S, THIS DAY, ORDER  WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
 -2-  NC: 2024:KHC-K:5962  CRL.P No. 200935 of 2024 CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE S.VISHWAJITH SHETTY  ORAL ORDER (PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE S.VISHWAJITH SHETTY)
1. Accused No.11 in CC No.7240/2023 pending on the file of III Addl. Civil Judge and JMFC,
Vijayapura, arising out of Crime No.83/2023 registered by the Vijayapura CEN Crime Police Station, Vijayapura for the offences punishable under Sections 66(C), 66(D) of Information Technology Act, 2008, Sections 419 and 420 of IPC and Section 14(a)(b) of Foreigners Act, 1946, is before this Court under Section 439 of Cr.P.C seeking regular bail.
2. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.

entities.text: Vijayapura CEN Crime Police Station, Vijayapura
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 3. FIR in Crime No.83/2023 was registered by the Vijayapura CEN Crime Police Station, Vijayapura against the unknown persons initially for the aforesaid offences on the basis of the first information received from Vishalkumar Jain S/o Ravindra.

entities.text: Vijayapura CEN Crime Police Station, Vijayapura
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: In the first information, it was alleged that some unknown persons with an intention to cheat the first informant had induced him to invest in crypto mining with an assurance NC: 2024:KHC-K:5962 that he would receive 200% profit and accordingly, from his bank account he had paid a total sum of `59,12,765/- to the account of the unknown persons.
During the course of investigation of the case, petitioner was arrested on 11.11.2023.
Investigation in the case is completed and charge- sheet has been filed as against 13 persons and petitioner herein is arrayed as accused No.11 in the charge-sheet.
Bail application filed by the petitioner before the jurisdictional Sessions Court in Crl.Misc.No.212/2024 was rejected by order dated 22.02.2024.
Therefore, he is before this Court.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner having reiterated the grounds urged in the petition submits that the petitioner is a citizens of Nigeria and he had come to India for business purpose.
The alleged offences against the petitioner are triable by the Court of Magistrate and maximum punishment for the alleged offence is imprisonment for a period of seven years.
He submits that the petitioner is ready to cooperate with the trial Court for expeditious disposal of the case.

Accordingly,
he prays to allow the petition.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent/State has opposed the petition.
In the event, the petitioner is enlarged on bail, he is likely to flee from justice.

Accordingly,
prays to dismiss the petition.

6. Allegation in the charge-sheet is that the accused persons were inducing people through social media for investment in crypto mining with an assurance that they would be getting 200% profit and in the present case, at various stages, accused persons totally collected a sum of `59,12,765/-
from the first informant, thereafter they had not returned the investment made by the first informant nor paid any profit as assured and thereby they allegedly had committed the alleged offences.
7. Undisputedly the alleged offences are triable by the Court of the Magistrate and maximum punishment for the alleged offences is imprisonment for a period of seven years.

Since the petitioner herein and some of the other accused are foreigners, Section 14(a) and 14(b) of the Foreigners Act,
1946 is also invoked in the charge-sheet against the said accused persons.
In the present case investigation is completed and NC: 2024:KHC-K:5962 petitioner herein who is arrayed as accused No.11 is in custody from 11.11.2023.

8. The Coordinate Bench of this Court in the case of Babul Khan and another vs State of Karnataka and another1 has laid down certain guidelines to be followed by the State Authorities and the Courts while considering the bail application of the foreign nationals.

entities.text: Babul Khan and another vs State of Karnataka and another1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relevant guidelines which would be material to the case on hand as found in para No.113 reads as under :
"(4) If for any reason the Court grants bail including anticipatory bail, in any criminal case where the offender is a foreign national, and the offences are under the Foreigners Act and/or also under any other Laws for the time being in force, and their Visa is cancelled or lapsed, or they have no Passport, or they are illegal migrants

, then the Courts shall specifically order to keep them in detention centers,
unless the competent authority has passed any order under section 3(2)(a) to (f) of Foreigners Act, 1946, or till further orders of the court or till they are deported to their mother country.

2020 SCC Online Kar 3438 NC: 2024:KHC-K:5962 (5) If the case registered against the foreign nationals, ended in conviction, they shall be ordered to be kept in regular prison of the State till they serve their sentence, and after serving the sentence, they shall be kept in detention centers till, they are deported to their country.
(6) If the case ends up in discharge, release of the accused or acquittal, and their nationality is in dispute before the competent Tribunal, they shall be ordered to be kept in detention centers till they are deported to their country unless they have any right or otherwise entitled to remain in India, or the competent authority has passed any orders under section 3(2)(a) to (e) of Foreigners Act 1946,
the acquittal, discharge or release of the accused is no bar for the concerned competent authorities Osmadiamen @ Peter Visa vs The State Of Karnataka on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56541611/
3 to question the nationality of that person before the competent Tribunal.

entities.text: Osmadiamen @ Peter Visa vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (7) The Public Prosecutors, the defence Counsel and the Courts shall make all their efforts to expeditiously deal with such cases by giving priority, for its early disposal, so as to enable other competent authorities to take appropriate steps under the facts and circumstances of each case for deportation of such foreign national (accused) as early as possible.

The Court may also if permissible under law, and applicable to the facts and circumstances of a case may invoke sections 265A NC:
2024:KHC-K:5962 to 265L under chapter XXI (A) of Code of Criminal procedure, after following due procedure."
9.

In the said case, the Coordinate Bench of this Court has observed that in the event the Court comes to the conclusion that the accused who is a foreign national, has made out a prima facie case for enlarging him on bail, the accused shall be directed to be detained in a detention center till the trial in the case is concluded.

10. Considering the case that the alleged offences in the present case are triable by the Court of Magistrate and the maximum punishment for the alleged offences is imprisonment for a period of seven years, I am of the opinion that the petitioner who is in custody from 11.11.2023 has made out a prima facie case for grant of regular bail.

Accordingly, the following:-
ORDER
The petition is allowed.
